themes.headline: You built a fast product… that your team now hates maintaining.
themes.body: Users love the experience. Engineers have started updating their LinkedIn profiles. The codebase is technically running. For now.

themes.headline: Users loved it… until it collapsed under scale.
themes.body: The product worked, in the way that things work before they don't. The system was always one bad deploy away from this. You just didn't look down.

themes.headline: Clean code. No users.
themes.body: The architecture is beautiful. The codebase is a gift to whoever inherits it. Nobody is using it. There's a difference between building well and building something people need.

themes.headline: You managed risk well… but never shipped anything meaningful.
themes.body: The system is stable. Extensible, even. No one uses it. There's a difference between building for the long term and never arriving at the present.

themes.headline: Users are happy. Engineers are not.
themes.body: The metrics look fine from the outside. Inside, everyone knows the truth. The team is tired. The system is fragile. You got away with it this time.

themes.headline: Nobody is using it.
themes.body: You made technically defensible choices at every turn. Users didn't care about the architecture. They just stopped coming back.

themes.headline: A workable product. The team is tired but intact.
themes.body: Not perfect. Not broken. You made real trade-offs and mostly got them right. The engineers are still here. That counts for something.

themes.headline: You built a product. It exists.
themes.body: The trade-offs are yours to live with. Every decision made sense at the time. That's the engineering experience.
